note: For any real orthogonal A with no eigenvalue 1: complex eigenvalues have modulus one; nonreal roots pair with conjugates and contribute product one; real roots are then all -1. If r is their multiplicity, n-r is even, so det A=(-1)^r=(-1)^n. For Q this gives det Q=(-1)^n. H acts by -1 on span(u) and +1 on u-perp, hence is orthogonal with det H=-1. Thus A=HQ is orthogonal with det A=(-1)^(n+1). Were 1 absent from its spectrum, the parity lemma would instead give (-1)^n, contradiction. Singularity of A-I over R supplies nonzero real w.
